note: Implementation readings of protocol.json where its text leaves a choice open. All were fixed before any post-entry return or quote sample was computed (see deviations.json D1 for the one trial that computed exits, deleted unread). Code cites these ids.

clarifications.C1: Entry 'within 5 minutes of t' means a bar starting before t + 5 minutes.
clarifications.C2: The halt flag counts runs of 5+ bar-less minutes between max(entry, 09:30) and 16:00, including the run before the first bar and after the last bar.
clarifications.C3: Cost time buckets are [04:00, 08:00), [08:00, 09:30), [09:30, 10:00) and [10:00, 16:00]. The protocol writes the second as 08:00-09:25, which leaves the 09:25 rule's entries (09:25-09:29 bars) without a bucket.
clarifications.C4: Regime: the 20-session mean and the 20-session realised volatility (standard deviation of 20 daily log returns) end at the previous session; the 252-session median is over that volatility series ending at the previous session. The SPY history window is deviation D4.
clarifications.C5: The cost sample holds the entries the loosest rule (G 0.20, V $250k, any news) fires that have an entry fill; every rule's fired entries are a subset of these. An entry is sampled when int.from_bytes(sha256('symbol|session|HH:MM').digest()[:8], 'big') % 20 == 0, with HH:MM the rule time.
clarifications.C6: Net return at notional N: shares q = N / entry; basis = q x entry x (1 + c_in) (+ IBKR commission); proceeds = q x exit x (1 - c_out) - SEC fee - FINRA TAF (- IBKR commission); net = proceeds / basis - 1. Trade-level metrics use N = $20,000 ($100k across 5 positions at 1x); fractional shares; fees are not rounded to the cent.
clarifications.C7: Stress doubles each side's spread-plus-slippage cost; regulatory fees and commissions are unchanged.
clarifications.C8: The break-even multiple is the k at which the mean net return with k x (spread + slippage) and unchanged fees is 0, found by bisection on [0, 1000]; null when the mean is at or below 0 at k = 0.
clarifications.C9: For a bucket still below 30 samples after the time x price fallback, 'the table's 90th percentile' is the 90th percentile (linear) of the table's own values: every cell with a measured trimmed mean (>= 30 samples) or a time x price fallback value. The pooled per-sample 90th percentile is reported beside it. (Amended after the pre-outcome review; the first reading used the pooled samples.)
clarifications.C10: The 5%-trimmed mean drops floor(0.05 n) samples from each tail.
clarifications.C11: Bootstrap: circular block bootstrap of 5 consecutive sessions over the split's full session calendar (sessions without trades included). Returns are quantised to 1e-6 so replicate sums are exact in floating point. A replicate with no trades counts as mean <= 0. Seed = int.from_bytes(sha256(b'mover-early-entry-v1-20260924').digest()[:8], 'big') with numpy default_rng (PCG64); one replicate matrix per split is shared by every rule-exit. The one-sided lower bound is the 5th percentile of the replicate means.
clarifications.C12: 'Mean without the top 5 sessions' drops every trade in the 5 sessions with the highest summed net return. The top 1% share is the sum of the top ceil(0.01 n) net returns over the total net sum (null when the total is <= 0). Profit factor = sum of gains / |sum of losses| (null without losses). Percentiles are numpy linear; the 1%-winsorised mean clips at the 1st and 99th percentiles.
clarifications.C13: The concurrent-fire count is the number of symbols the same rule fires in the same session (fires, filled or not), grouped 1, 2-5, 6-20, >20. V tiers are $250k-1M, $1-5M and >= $5M of dollar_volume_at_t.
clarifications.C14: Two-way clustering: V = V_session + V_symbol - V_symbol-day for the mean, with max(V_session, V_symbol) when negative; one-sided normal p.
clarifications.C15: Portfolio: equity marked at t equals the session's starting equity (each rule enters at one time and holds nothing overnight). Sub-$5 names use min(leverage, 1). Capacity uses the entry bar's dollar volume (the opening auction: the listing exchange's opening print price x size). Fees use each position's actual notional. Drawdown is measured at each session start against the running peak of session-end equity: factor 1 within 10%, 0.5 within 10-20%; beyond 20% a 10-session no-entry cooldown starts, after which 0.5 applies; the cooldown re-arms only after the drawdown has returned within 20%.
clarifications.C16: IWM's official open-to-close uses official_price on IWM's auctions (fetched with asof 2026-09-21); it stands in for every holding window and is flagged as a proxy.
clarifications.C17: The placebo enters at t + 30 minutes under the entry rule for that time (09:00 + 30 is the 09:30 opening auction).
clarifications.C18: Capture: per degree tier, time, G, V and news variant. Recall 'among days meeting price and volume' conditions on price_t >= $1 and dollar_volume_at_t >= V. An undefined gain_at_t does not fire. The entry-to-close and entry-to-session-high returns are gross.
clarifications.C19: Replication: gain_at_09:25 uses bars starting before 09:25; an undefined gain counts as below 0.20; Spearman uses average ranks over days with a defined gain.
clarifications.C20: Paper-candidate tie-break for 'the most-traded development rule-exit': trades descending, then development p ascending, then rule id.
clarifications.C21: Coverage: an audit event (verdict match or recovered_match, official gain >= +20%) is present when (symbol_used, date) or (ticker, date) is a candidate; tiers use the audit's official gain.
clarifications.C22: The session close used by X1, the X2-X4 close fallbacks and eventual_gain is the official close, else the daily bar close (the price audit's v2 fallback; D3 measured it equal to the official close on 92% of days), else the last bar close before the session close, else the entry price, each flagged. (Amended after the pre-outcome review; the first reading skipped the daily close.)
clarifications.C23: When the previous session has no official close, ref uses the daily dataset's previous raw close, flagged (the daily close is the official closing print on 92% of sampled days; deviations.json D3).
clarifications.C24: Portfolio slots rank every fire of the rule (filled or not) by dollar_volume_at_t, then symbol, since whether an entry fills is not known at t. A fire without a fill keeps its slot with zero P&L and counts in the desired notional. Trade-level statistics use filled entries.
clarifications.C25: A rule fires when gain_at_t >= G - 1e-9, so that a price of exactly (1 + G) x ref (for example 6.00 over 5.00) fires despite binary rounding of price / ref - 1.
clarifications.C26: The protocol's 16:00 (exit window end, X1 time, halt-flag window, bar-close fallback) is the session's close: 13:00 ET on NYSE scheduled early closes (12 in 2021-2026, from exchange_calendars 4.13.2's XNYS schedule, listed in rules.EARLY_CLOSES). The cost sample's 15:55 stamp is 5 minutes before that close (named close-5m).
clarifications.C27: The holdout's at most five validated rule-exits are the lowest validation p, then the higher validation lower bound, then rule id (the bootstrap p has a floor of 1/20001, so strong rule-exits can tie on p).
clarifications.C28: The one-sided lower bound is the order statistic at index floor(0.05 x (B - 1)) of the sorted replicate means, with replicates that have no trades counted as minus infinity (the bound is null when more than 5% of replicates are empty). The evaluator checks the runtime pins, the daily dataset, the main list and the D3 supplement against their recorded hashes, and records the sha256 of the cost table, fees, clarifications, deviations and the audit file.
clarifications.C29: The 'BH across all 768 rule-exits' sensitivity is reported at both stages: development p BH-adjusted across all 768 at <= 0.05 with >= 200 trades, and validation p BH-adjusted across all 768 at <= 0.10 with >= 100 trades and the three positive robustness means. Neither changes selection.
clarifications.C30: After the holdout, the paper candidate is the evaluated rule-exit with the highest holdout lower bound (paper_e2e's first clause); it is labelled mechanics-only unless it passed the holdout. Holdout statistics are computed only for the evaluated rule-exits.
clarifications.C31: Live scanning waits for the rule's signal cutoff (09:28 for the 09:30 rule). Because the 09:27 bar closes at the 09:28 on-open order cutoff, a live 09:30 signal cannot be completed in time to submit an opening-auction order, so 09:30 rule-exits are not paper candidates (the study still evaluates them); the paper candidate is the best-ranked non-09:30 rule-exit under the same order.
clarifications.C32: Outcomes mode requires the committed cost table (its sha256 is stored in the outcome meta and checked by the evaluator); any holdout read requires the dev_val results (sha256 stored and checked). Collections are refused when any run used an asof other than 2026-09-21 or when a session's collected symbol count differs from the frozen list; every ledger page must have its file.
